analyst: Manual analysis using Claude Opus 5.5 for verification and code analysis

servers.code_repo: https://github.com/heroku/heroku-mcp-server (local stdio server; the remote server at the CSV endpoint is closed)
servers.mcp_version: Local: @modelcontextprotocol/sdk 1.32.1 (TypeScript SDK v1, up to 2025-11-25); remote: not published
servers.server_cost: Free (Apache 2.0 code; remote: no price given)
servers.linked_cost: No free plan: Eco dyno $5/month (sleeps), Basic $7, Standard-1X $25, Performance-M $250; Postgres Essential-0 $5/month
servers.restrictions: Rights = the Heroku account's rights (local: CLI token / HEROKU_API_KEY; remote: OAuth). Local: Heroku CLI >= 10.8.1. Remote in Claude Team/Enterprise: only users with the permission can add the server. Status: "currently in early development".
servers.governance_logic: 1) Wrapper around the Heroku CLI in REPL mode; CLI restarted on timeout. 2) Error text tells the AI to "Ignore any Heroku CLI command suggestions" and use only MCP tools. 3) File path validation in deploy_one_off_dyno. 4) AI tools registered only with the plugin. 5) No restrictions on dangerous actions: pg_psql runs any SQL, pg_kill kills DB processes, pg_upgrade only has a confirm parameter filled by the AI; no read-only mode, no annotations. 6) Logging hook stub "(not-implemented)".
servers.structure_note: Flat; the local (open) and remote (closed) servers are different implementations
servers.actions_comment: Local: 36 (33 without the AI plugin). Docs list transfer_app, which is not in the code. Remote: not published ("first set of tools": apps, teams/spaces, add-on marketplace).
servers.token_method: ~2,900 for descriptions + the app.json JSON schema embedded in deploy_to_heroku; characters / 4
servers.agent_cannot: Delete apps and add-ons; manage domains, config vars, collaborators, billing; roll back releases. The remote server started with an even smaller set.
servers.docs_recs: Use heroku mcp:start so as not to expose the API key. Nothing about confirming dangerous actions (SQL, scaling).
servers.gov_promises: Remote: "enhanced security", "full control over which applications can access your resources", consent to the tool set - no technical details.
servers.user_promises: "Secure and authenticated access to Heroku Platform APIs"
servers.promises_vs_logic: Security promises are general; the local code has no protection for dangerous tools (arbitrary SQL, pg_kill).
servers.notes: The CSV endpoint is the remote server (closed); the code analysis and the Actions sheet refer to the local server (package version 1.2.12). Actions generated from the appendix 16b; types derived from tool names (no annotations) and corrected by hand.

Tools.desc: Local: 36 tools (33 + 3 AI tools registered only with @heroku/plugin-ai); no annotations; capabilities.tools.listChanged: true. Remote: not published.
Tools.post: Heroku CLI text output as is; on error isError and the prefix "[Heroku MCP Server Error] Please use available tools to resolve this issue. Ignore any Heroku CLI command suggestions ..."

Authorization.desc: Local: Heroku CLI token or HEROKU_API_KEY (no authorization to the MCP server itself). Remote: OAuth 2.0 via id.heroku.com; metadata documents; DCR (https://mcp.heroku.com/reg); grants authorization_code, refresh_token, device_code; PKCE S256; scopes openid, offline_access; the user can "consent to which tools a client can access".

Error Reporting.desc: isError with the redirecting prefix; fatal CLI errors -> process exits

observations.text: Dangerous tools without protection: arbitrary SQL in the production database and killing processes - no annotations, no read-only mode, no server-side confirmation. Sharp contrast with Grafana, where raw SQL is disabled in read-only mode.
A server as a wrapper around the CLI: the agent's capabilities are a subset of the CLI.
Divergence between documentation and code (transfer_app is documented but does not exist).
Device code grant in the remote server's OAuth - sign-in without a browser on the same device.
